Elect Katie Hobbs, 2026 election cycle: raised $11,109,719.95; spent $14,355,612.69. Filed with the Arizona Secretary of State — See The Money; read September 8th, 2026.

Arizona Secretary of State — See The Money · Read September 8th, 2026

Our canonical officeholder records could not be read for this answer. This is a holding failure, not a finding that there are no officials for this place or person.

Arizona's legislature lists 264 bills that became law in the 57leg/2r session. We have read 29 of them so far, so anything here about bills she signed is a partial account and not the whole session.

She also sent the legislature 151 letters about individual bills. We have retrieved 1 of those letters and have not been able to read 1 of them — they are scanned images and we do not yet have text recognition for them. We hold the documents and can link you to them, but we will not say what any of them decided until we have read it.

We read 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, and the index continues past what we walked.

We have not established a canonical voting-office identity for Katie Hobbs, so no other person's voting record has been attached.

County filings: no applicable county filing was resolved for this answer about Katie Hobbs. That does not establish that none exists.

State filings: this answer uses the same state campaign-money records as the card. These records describe the campaigns' own filings; they do not establish outside spending for or against Katie Hobbs.

Federal filings: no applicable FEC record was resolved for this answer. This does not establish an absence of state or county filings.

HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. meetings.minutes: Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. It removed all five members of the county's Industrial Development Authority board without cause, approved a new structure for that authority, and elected new members. It also approved the River Overlook rezoning and comprehensive-plan amendment on West River Road (5–0) and two cell-tower permits, updated the county's air-quality code to match current federal rules, denied a wholesale liquor license on East Cabeza De Vaca Street (zoning there does not allow wholesale), and — sitting as the Library District board — accepted a $7,500 grant for a local-news pilot program (4–1), among other business.

Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 9/1/2026

documents.text: Tucson Unified Governing Board Next Meeting View the Governing Board Meeting Live. Governing Board Meeting 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm × Governing Board Meeting Date & Time: 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm Governing Board meetings are held at the Duffy Community Center, 5145 E. 5 th Street, 85711, in the Multipurpose Room. All meeting notices, agendas, minutes, actions, recordings, and other resources are available on Diligent Community . Audio-video recordings are available shortly after the meetings also on Diligent Community . Close Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Special Meeting on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. To access agenda items and support materials go to Diligent Community . Recordings Audio-video recordings are available after the meetings on Diligent Community just choose the meeting you wish to view and then select video. Vacancies Events with 3 or More Members Impact Tucson Community and Family Resource Fair - July 25, 2026 Proclamations Resolutions National School Counseling Week Proclamation - February 2-6, 2026 Career & Technical Education (CTE) Month Proclamation - February 2026 Purchasing Month Proclamation - March 2026 Social Worker Month Proclamation - March 2026 Live Meeting Videos Governing Board meetings will be available here when meetings are in session. August 11, 2026 Meeting Vote to Convene On district Windows devices, students and staff may find that these videos on YouTube are blocked. If so, please log into Google with your district credentials . Error Message: For more details and instructions, please visit our TS Article on YouTube Videos (Sharepoint) . Thank you for your patience, as we work to resolve this.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries regulated by the health department. Public use and driving under its influence remain illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to attend school or child care; Arizona allows medical and personal-belief exemptions with the state form.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Adults 21 and over who may legally own a firearm can carry it openly or concealed without a permit. An optional concealed-weapons permit exists, mainly for other states' recognition and certain locations.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — Arizona has a flat state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Department of Revenue.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: Arizona expects new residents to get an Arizona license and register their vehicles promptly once residency is established — there is no fixed grace period, so the Motor Vehicle Division is an early errand.
facts.sourceOrg: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online or by mail at least 29 days before an election. Arizona voters show identification at the polls.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are billed by your county and fund schools, county, city, and district services; state law limits how fast a home's taxable value can grow, and qualifying seniors can apply to freeze their valuation.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. Arizona Game and Fish requires anyone 10 or older — resident or not — to hold a valid licence to take wildlife, fish included. People who live in Arizona pay less for one than visitors do.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: Arizona's constitution gives every person a fundamental right to abortion. Before the point a treating health professional judges the fetus could survive outside the womb, the state may restrict it only for a compelling health reason. After that point, it may not block an abortion that professional judges necessary to protect the pregnant person's life or health.

billSummary.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
billSummary.summary: A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries. Using it in public or driving under its influence remains illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need a set of routine immunizations to attend school or child care; New Jersey allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Carrying a handgun requires a Permit to Carry issued through the State Police, with training and application requirements; buying any firearm requires a purchaser identification card or pistol purchase permit.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — New Jersey has a graduated state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Division of Taxation.

facts.question: How long do I have to transfer my license and registration?
facts.answer: Within 60 days of moving in, or before your current license and registration expire — whichever comes first — through the Motor Vehicle Commission.

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online, by mail, or in person at least 21 days before an election. New Jersey mails every registered voter information about voting options each election.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are set and billed by your municipality and fund schools, county, and local services. The state's ANCHOR program pays a property-tax relief benefit to eligible homeowners and renters.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Jersey law requires a licence to hunt or trap at any age, and anyone over 16 needs one to fish the state's fresh waters with a rod and line. Saltwater fishing is registered separately rather than licensed.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 23:3-1 (Licence for hunting, fishing, trapping)

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Jersey law states a fundamental right to choose whether to carry a pregnancy, to give birth, or to end one. The Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act sets no time limit and requires no waiting period.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 10:7-2 (Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act)

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register with your town or city clerk ahead of time, or at the polls on election day itself. Bring proof of who you are, your age, your citizenship, and where you live.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are the main way New Hampshire towns and schools are funded, set town by town; the annual town meeting votes the budget that drives the rate. Credits and exemptions (veterans, elderly, disabled) run through your town.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Hampshire law says nobody may fish, hunt or trap in the state without first getting a valid licence, and it has to be carried while you are doing it. The same chapter sets out the exceptions, including some for young people.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy. From 24 weeks a provider may not perform one except in a medical emergency, and must first determine the likely gestational age. There is no time limit written into state law before that point.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire RSA 329:44 (Fetal Life Protection Act — Prohibition)

Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, August 25, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 8/19/2026

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/27/2026

CALL TO THE PUBLIC
Individuals wishing to participate telephonically at Call to the Public must contact the Clerk of the Board’s Office at 520-724-8449, to register their request and obtain remote access information, by the deadline of Monday, July 27, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Call to the Public shall be scheduled for one hour each meeting unless extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. Speakers shall have up to three minutes to speak. However, for any meeting where 20 or more individuals have submitted speaker cards, each speaker's time shall be limited to two minutes. Please be aware that you may not be called upon to speak if the time for Call to the Public expires and is not extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. eComments can also be submitted to COB_mail@pima.gov.

agenda.title:
Hearing - Specific Plan and Comprehensive Plan Amendment
P26SP00001, RIVER OVERLOOK, L.L.C. - W. RIVER ROAD SPECIFIC PLAN AND COMPREHENSIVE PLAN AMENDMENT
River Overlook, L.L.C., represented by Projects International, Inc., requests a comprehensive plan amendment and specific plan rezoning for approximately 4.2 acres (Parcel Codes 104-01-040H, 104-01-0460, 104-01-0470, 104-01-048C, 104-01-040L together with a portion of 104-01-042B and 104-01-0450, as well as a portion of abandoned right-of-way of W. River Terrace Drive) to amend the Comprehensive Plan from Medium Intensity Urban (MIU) and Commercial Activity Center (CAC) to Planned Development Community (PDC) and to rezone from SH (Suburban Homestead) to SP (Specific Plan) zone. The site is located on the south side of W. River Road, approximately one-quarter mile west of N. La Canada Drive, in Section 15, T13S, R13E, in the Catalina Foothills Planning Area. On motion, the Planning and Zoning Commission voted 5-1 (Commissioner Hanna voted NAY, Commissioners Hook, Maese, Matter and Tronsdal were absent) to recommended APPROVAL SUBJECT TO STANDARD AND SPECIAL CONDITIONS WITH AN ADDITIONAL CONDITION. Staff recommends APPROVAL OF THE SPECIFIC PLAN AND COMPREHENSIVE PLAN AMENDMENT. (District 1 3)

meetings.minutes: Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. It removed all five members of the county's Industrial Development Authority board without cause, approved a new structure for that authority, and elected new members. It also approved the River Overlook rezoning and comprehensive-plan amendment on West River Road (5–0) and two cell-tower permits, updated the county's air-quality code to match current federal rules, denied a wholesale liquor license on East Cabeza De Vaca Street (zoning there does not allow wholesale), and — sitting as the Library District board — accepted a $7,500 grant for a local-news pilot program (4–1), among other business.

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. agenda.title:
Hearing - Rezoning
P26RZ00001, REED - N. PONTATOC ROAD REZONING 
James Frederick Reed, represented by Demion Clinco of the Tucson Historic Preservation Foundation, requests a rezoning of approximately 0.93 acres from the CR-1 (Single Residence) zone to the CR-1 (HL) (Single Residence - Historic Landmark) zone, on property located on the west side of N. Pontatoc Road, approximately 115 feet north of the intersection of N. Pontatoc Road and E. Saranac Drive, addressed as 4239 N. Pontatoc Road. The proposed rezoning conforms to the Pima County Comprehensive Plan which designates the property for Low Intensity Urban 1.2. On motion, the Planning and Zoning Commission voted 6 - 0 (Commissioners Cook, Gungle, Becker and Maese were absent) to recommend APPROVAL SUBJECT TO STANDARD AND SPECIAL CONDITIONS. Staff recommends APPROVAL SUBJECT TO STANDARD AND SPECIAL CONDITIONS. (District 1)

Governing Board Meeting 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm × Governing Board Meeting Date & Time: 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm Governing Board meetings are held at the Duffy Community Center, 5145 E. 5 th Street, 85711, in the Multipurpose Room. All meeting notices, agendas, minutes, actions, recordings, and other resources are available on Diligent Community . Audio-video recordings are available shortly after the meetings also on Diligent Community . Close Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Special Meeting on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries regulated by the health department. Public use and driving under its influence remain illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to attend school or child care; Arizona allows medical and personal-belief exemptions with the state form.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Adults 21 and over who may legally own a firearm can carry it openly or concealed without a permit. An optional concealed-weapons permit exists, mainly for other states' recognition and certain locations.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — Arizona has a flat state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Department of Revenue.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: Arizona expects new residents to get an Arizona license and register their vehicles promptly once residency is established — there is no fixed grace period, so the Motor Vehicle Division is an early errand.
facts.sourceOrg: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online or by mail at least 29 days before an election. Arizona voters show identification at the polls.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are billed by your county and fund schools, county, city, and district services; state law limits how fast a home's taxable value can grow, and qualifying seniors can apply to freeze their valuation.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. Arizona Game and Fish requires anyone 10 or older — resident or not — to hold a valid licence to take wildlife, fish included. People who live in Arizona pay less for one than visitors do.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: Arizona's constitution gives every person a fundamental right to abortion. Before the point a treating health professional judges the fetus could survive outside the womb, the state may restrict it only for a compelling health reason. After that point, it may not block an abortion that professional judges necessary to protect the pregnant person's life or health.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: Arizona expects new residents to get an Arizona license and register their vehicles promptly once residency is established — there is no fixed grace period, so the Motor Vehicle Division is an early errand.
facts.sourceOrg: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online or by mail at least 29 days before an election. Arizona voters show identification at the polls.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are billed by your county and fund schools, county, city, and district services; state law limits how fast a home's taxable value can grow, and qualifying seniors can apply to freeze their valuation.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. Arizona Game and Fish requires anyone 10 or older — resident or not — to hold a valid licence to take wildlife, fish included. People who live in Arizona pay less for one than visitors do.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: Arizona's constitution gives every person a fundamental right to abortion. Before the point a treating health professional judges the fetus could survive outside the womb, the state may restrict it only for a compelling health reason. After that point, it may not block an abortion that professional judges necessary to protect the pregnant person's life or health.

billSummary.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
billSummary.summary: A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries. Using it in public or driving under its influence remains illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need a set of routine immunizations to attend school or child care; New Jersey allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Carrying a handgun requires a Permit to Carry issued through the State Police, with training and application requirements; buying any firearm requires a purchaser identification card or pistol purchase permit.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — New Jersey has a graduated state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Division of Taxation.

facts.question: How long do I have to transfer my license and registration?
facts.answer: Within 60 days of moving in, or before your current license and registration expire — whichever comes first — through the Motor Vehicle Commission.

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online, by mail, or in person at least 21 days before an election. New Jersey mails every registered voter information about voting options each election.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are set and billed by your municipality and fund schools, county, and local services. The state's ANCHOR program pays a property-tax relief benefit to eligible homeowners and renters.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Jersey law requires a licence to hunt or trap at any age, and anyone over 16 needs one to fish the state's fresh waters with a rod and line. Saltwater fishing is registered separately rather than licensed.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 23:3-1 (Licence for hunting, fishing, trapping)

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Jersey law states a fundamental right to choose whether to carry a pregnancy, to give birth, or to end one. The Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act sets no time limit and requires no waiting period.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 10:7-2 (Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act)

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Recreational marijuana is not legal. Possessing three-quarters of an ounce or less is a civil violation (a fine, not a crime), and a state-run therapeutic cannabis program serves qualifying patients.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows anyone who may legally own a handgun to carry it openly or concealed without a license. An optional pistol/revolver license exists, mainly for carrying in other states that honor it.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: No — New Hampshire does not tax wages, and its separate tax on interest and dividends was repealed effective 2025. There is also no state sales tax.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: New residents have 60 days after establishing residency to register vehicles and get a New Hampshire driver's license. Registration runs through your town clerk plus the DMV.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register with your town or city clerk ahead of time, or at the polls on election day itself. Bring proof of who you are, your age, your citizenship, and where you live.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are the main way New Hampshire towns and schools are funded, set town by town; the annual town meeting votes the budget that drives the rate. Credits and exemptions (veterans, elderly, disabled) run through your town.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Hampshire law says nobody may fish, hunt or trap in the state without first getting a valid licence, and it has to be carried while you are doing it. The same chapter sets out the exceptions, including some for young people.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy. From 24 weeks a provider may not perform one except in a medical emergency, and must first determine the likely gestational age. There is no time limit written into state law before that point.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire RSA 329:44 (Fetal Life Protection Act — Prohibition)

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, August 25, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 8/19/2026
August 25, 2026 Board of Supervisors Meeting Agenda Clerk's Note: Members of the Pima County Board of Supervisors will attend either in person or by telephone, video or internet conferencing. The meeting can be streamed via the following links: BOS Agenda August 25, 2026 (http://pima.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?view_id=3), on YouTube (https://www.youtube.com/c/PimaCountyArizona/), or via Cox Cable Channel 96. Television viewing will be available in the lobby at 130 West Congress, 1st Floor. 1. ROLL CALL 2. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 3. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT To be offered by Robert Ojeda, CEO, Pima Council on Aging. 4. CURRENT EVENTS/PUBLIC ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS 5. AGENDA ADJUSTMENTS 6. CALL TO THE PUBLIC Individuals wishing to participate telephonically at Call to the Public must contact the Clerk of the Board’s Office at 520-724-8449, to register their request and obtain remote access information, by the deadline of Monday, August 24, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. Call to the Public shall be scheduled for one hour each meeting unless extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. Speakers shall have up to three minutes to speak. However, for any meeting where 20 or more individuals have submitted speaker cards, each speaker's time shall be limited to two minutes. Please be aware that you may not be called upon to speak if the time for Call to the Public expires and is not extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. eComments can also be submitted to COB_mail@pima.gov. EXECUTIVE SESSION (Clerk's Note: As of the posting date of 8/19/26, no executive session item has been placed on the regular agenda. However, this is subject to any addendum. Pursuant to A.R.S. §38-431.03(A)(3) the Board of Supervisors, or the Board sitting as other boards, may vote to go into executive session for the purpose of obtaining legal advice from its counsel with respect to any item listed on this agenda or any addendum thereto.) Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/27/2026

Speakers shall have up to three minutes to speak. However, for any meeting where 20 or more individuals have submitted speaker cards, each speaker's time shall be limited to two minutes. Please be aware that you may not be called upon to speak if the time for Call to the Public expires and is not extended by a majority vote of the Board of Supervisors. eComments can also be submitted to COB_mail@pima.gov.

Hearing - Specific Plan and Comprehensive Plan Amendment
P26SP00001, RIVER OVERLOOK, L.L.C. - W. RIVER ROAD SPECIFIC PLAN AND COMPREHENSIVE PLAN AMENDMENT
River Overlook, L.L.C., represented by Projects International, Inc., requests a comprehensive plan amendment and specific plan rezoning for approximately 4.2 acres (Parcel Codes 104-01-040H, 104-01-0460, 104-01-0470, 104-01-048C, 104-01-040L together with a portion of 104-01-042B and 104-01-0450, as well as a portion of abandoned right-of-way of W. River Terrace Drive) to amend the Comprehensive Plan from Medium Intensity Urban (MIU) and Commercial Activity Center (CAC) to Planned Development Community (PDC) and to rezone from SH (Suburban Homestead) to SP (Specific Plan) zone. The site is located on the south side of W. River Road, approximately one-quarter mile west of N. La Canada Drive, in Section 15, T13S, R13E, in the Catalina Foothills Planning Area. On motion, the Planning and Zoning Commission voted 5-1 (Commissioner Hanna voted NAY, Commissioners Hook, Maese, Matter and Tronsdal were absent) to recommended APPROVAL SUBJECT TO STANDARD AND SPECIAL CONDITIONS WITH AN ADDITIONAL CONDITION. Staff recommends APPROVAL OF THE SPECIFIC PLAN AND COMPREHENSIVE PLAN AMENDMENT. (District 1 3)

meetings.minutes: Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. It removed all five members of the county's Industrial Development Authority board without cause, approved a new structure for that authority, and elected new members. It also approved the River Overlook rezoning and comprehensive-plan amendment on West River Road (5–0) and two cell-tower permits, updated the county's air-quality code to match current federal rules, denied a wholesale liquor license on East Cabeza De Vaca Street (zoning there does not allow wholesale), and — sitting as the Library District board — accepted a $7,500 grant for a local-news pilot program (4–1), among other business.

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, September 8, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. P26RZ00001, REED - N. PONTATOC ROAD REZONING 
James Frederick Reed, represented by Demion Clinco of the Tucson Historic Preservation Foundation, requests a rezoning of approximately 0.93 acres from the CR-1 (Single Residence) zone to the CR-1 (HL) (Single Residence - Historic Landmark) zone, on property located on the west side of N. Pontatoc Road, approximately 115 feet north of the intersection of N. Pontatoc Road and E. Saranac Drive, addressed as 4239 N. Pontatoc Road. The proposed rezoning conforms to the Pima County Comprehensive Plan which designates the property for Low Intensity Urban 1.2. On motion, the Planning and Zoning Commission voted 6 - 0 (Commissioners Cook, Gungle, Becker and Maese were absent) to recommend APPROVAL SUBJECT TO STANDARD AND SPECIAL CONDITIONS. Staff recommends APPROVAL SUBJECT TO STANDARD AND SPECIAL CONDITIONS. (District 1)

documents.text: Tucson Unified Governing Board Next Meeting View the Governing Board Meeting Live. Governing Board Meeting 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm × Governing Board Meeting Date & Time: 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm Governing Board meetings are held at the Duffy Community Center, 5145 E. 5 th Street, 85711, in the Multipurpose Room. All meeting notices, agendas, minutes, actions, recordings, and other resources are available on Diligent Community . Audio-video recordings are available shortly after the meetings also on Diligent Community . Close Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Special Meeting on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. To access agenda items and support materials go to Diligent Community . Recordings Audio-video recordings are available after the meetings on Diligent Community just choose the meeting you wish to view and then select video. Vacancies Events with 3 or More Members Impact Tucson Community and Family Resource Fair - July 25, 2026 Proclamations Resolutions National School Counseling Week Proclamation - February 2-6, 2026 Career & Technical Education (CTE) Month Proclamation - February 2026 Purchasing Month Proclamation - March 2026 Social Worker Month Proclamation - March 2026 Live Meeting Videos Governing Board meetings will be available here when meetings are in session. August 11, 2026 Meeting Vote to Convene On district Windows devices, students and staff may find that these videos on YouTube are blocked. If so, please log into Google with your district credentials . Error Message: For more details and instructions, please visit our TS Article on YouTube Videos (Sharepoint) . Thank you for your patience, as we work to resolve this.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries regulated by the health department. Public use and driving under its influence remain illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to attend school or child care; Arizona allows medical and personal-belief exemptions with the state form.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Adults 21 and over who may legally own a firearm can carry it openly or concealed without a permit. An optional concealed-weapons permit exists, mainly for other states' recognition and certain locations.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — Arizona has a flat state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Department of Revenue.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: Arizona expects new residents to get an Arizona license and register their vehicles promptly once residency is established — there is no fixed grace period, so the Motor Vehicle Division is an early errand.
facts.sourceOrg: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online or by mail at least 29 days before an election. Arizona voters show identification at the polls.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are billed by your county and fund schools, county, city, and district services; state law limits how fast a home's taxable value can grow, and qualifying seniors can apply to freeze their valuation.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. Arizona Game and Fish requires anyone 10 or older — resident or not — to hold a valid licence to take wildlife, fish included. People who live in Arizona pay less for one than visitors do.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: Arizona's constitution gives every person a fundamental right to abortion. Before the point a treating health professional judges the fetus could survive outside the womb, the state may restrict it only for a compelling health reason. After that point, it may not block an abortion that professional judges necessary to protect the pregnant person's life or health.

billSummary.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
billSummary.summary: A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing.

meetings.minutes: The Board approved the minutes of its July 8 meetings and three permission requests, including street closings for Boonton's Labor Day parade. It adopted resolutions including an amendment extending the historic-preservation easement on the Pompton Plains Railroad Station to 2056. Two of the seven commissioners were absent. During public comment, residents raised the county's ADA grievance process and asked for updates on a homicide investigation. The Board opened with condolences on the death of longtime Boonton official Cy Wekilsky, among other business.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries. Using it in public or driving under its influence remains illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need a set of routine immunizations to attend school or child care; New Jersey allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Carrying a handgun requires a Permit to Carry issued through the State Police, with training and application requirements; buying any firearm requires a purchaser identification card or pistol purchase permit.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — New Jersey has a graduated state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Division of Taxation.

facts.question: How long do I have to transfer my license and registration?
facts.answer: Within 60 days of moving in, or before your current license and registration expire — whichever comes first — through the Motor Vehicle Commission.

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online, by mail, or in person at least 21 days before an election. New Jersey mails every registered voter information about voting options each election.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are set and billed by your municipality and fund schools, county, and local services. The state's ANCHOR program pays a property-tax relief benefit to eligible homeowners and renters.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Jersey law requires a licence to hunt or trap at any age, and anyone over 16 needs one to fish the state's fresh waters with a rod and line. Saltwater fishing is registered separately rather than licensed.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 23:3-1 (Licence for hunting, fishing, trapping)

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Jersey law states a fundamental right to choose whether to carry a pregnancy, to give birth, or to end one. The Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act sets no time limit and requires no waiting period.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 10:7-2 (Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act)

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Recreational marijuana is not legal. Possessing three-quarters of an ounce or less is a civil violation (a fine, not a crime), and a state-run therapeutic cannabis program serves qualifying patients.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to enroll in school or child care; New Hampshire allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows anyone who may legally own a handgun to carry it openly or concealed without a license. An optional pistol/revolver license exists, mainly for carrying in other states that honor it.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: No — New Hampshire does not tax wages, and its separate tax on interest and dividends was repealed effective 2025. There is also no state sales tax.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: New residents have 60 days after establishing residency to register vehicles and get a New Hampshire driver's license. Registration runs through your town clerk plus the DMV.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register with your town or city clerk ahead of time, or at the polls on election day itself. Bring proof of who you are, your age, your citizenship, and where you live.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are the main way New Hampshire towns and schools are funded, set town by town; the annual town meeting votes the budget that drives the rate. Credits and exemptions (veterans, elderly, disabled) run through your town.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Hampshire law says nobody may fish, hunt or trap in the state without first getting a valid licence, and it has to be carried while you are doing it. The same chapter sets out the exceptions, including some for young people.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy. From 24 weeks a provider may not perform one except in a medical emergency, and must first determine the likely gestational age. There is no time limit written into state law before that point.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire RSA 329:44 (Fetal Life Protection Act — Prohibition)

Board of Supervisors Pima County Meeting Agenda MEETING LOCATION Administration Bldg - East 130 W. Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/27/2026

meetings.minutes: Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. It removed all five members of the county's Industrial Development Authority board without cause, approved a new structure for that authority, and elected new members. It also approved the River Overlook rezoning and comprehensive-plan amendment on West River Road (5–0) and two cell-tower permits, updated the county's air-quality code to match current federal rules, denied a wholesale liquor license on East Cabeza De Vaca Street (zoning there does not allow wholesale), and — sitting as the Library District board — accepted a $7,500 grant for a local-news pilot program (4–1), among other business.

documents.text: Tucson Unified Governing Board Next Meeting View the Governing Board Meeting Live. Governing Board Meeting 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm × Governing Board Meeting Date & Time: 8/25/2026 4:30pm - 8:30pm Governing Board meetings are held at the Duffy Community Center, 5145 E. 5 th Street, 85711, in the Multipurpose Room. All meeting notices, agendas, minutes, actions, recordings, and other resources are available on Diligent Community . Audio-video recordings are available shortly after the meetings also on Diligent Community . Close Board Members Dr. Ravi Shah Email Dr. Ravi Shah Board President Term expires: December 31, 2028 Natalie Luna Rose Email Natalie Luna Rose Board Clerk Term expires: December 31, 2028 Jennifer Eckstrom Email Jennifer Eckstrom Term expires: December 31, 2026 Val Romero Email Val Romero Term Expires: December 31, 2026 Sadie Shaw Email Sadie Shaw Term expires: December 31, 2028 Current Members' Bios Members: 1867-Present (PDF) Contact the Board Email Governing Board ( [email protected] ) Phone: (520) 225-6070 FAX: (520) 798-8767 Policies for Review: When the Governing Board is soliciting feedback on policies proposed for elimination, revision, and adoption, please click here to: Share your feedback Board Meeting The Governing Board will hold a Special Meeting on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 with Executive Session beginning at 4:30 p.m. and the Public meeting scheduled to begin at 5:30 p.m. at the Duffy Community Center - Multipurpose Room, 5145 E. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. To access agenda items and support materials go to Diligent Community . Recordings Audio-video recordings are available after the meetings on Diligent Community just choose the meeting you wish to view and then select video. If so, please log into Google with your district credentials . Error Message: For more details and instructions, please visit our TS Article on YouTube Videos (Sharepoint) . Thank you for your patience, as we work to resolve this.

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries regulated by the health department. Public use and driving under its influence remain illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to attend school or child care; Arizona allows medical and personal-belief exemptions with the state form.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Adults 21 and over who may legally own a firearm can carry it openly or concealed without a permit. An optional concealed-weapons permit exists, mainly for other states' recognition and certain locations.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — Arizona has a flat state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Department of Revenue.

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: Arizona expects new residents to get an Arizona license and register their vehicles promptly once residency is established — there is no fixed grace period, so the Motor Vehicle Division is an early errand.
facts.sourceOrg: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online or by mail at least 29 days before an election. Arizona voters show identification at the polls.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are billed by your county and fund schools, county, city, and district services; state law limits how fast a home's taxable value can grow, and qualifying seniors can apply to freeze their valuation.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. Arizona Game and Fish requires anyone 10 or older — resident or not — to hold a valid licence to take wildlife, fish included. People who live in Arizona pay less for one than visitors do.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: Arizona's constitution gives every person a fundamental right to abortion. Before the point a treating health professional judges the fetus could survive outside the womb, the state may restrict it only for a compelling health reason. After that point, it may not block an abortion that professional judges necessary to protect the pregnant person's life or health.

billSummary.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
billSummary.summary: A stop-gap spending bill. It keeps the federal government funded — mostly at last year's levels — until December 11, 2026, or until the regular spending bills pass, whichever comes first, preventing a shutdown when the budget year starts October 1. It makes exceptions for programs like WIC food aid, small-business loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, and extends expiring programs covering agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, and housing.
