facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Yes — adults 21 and over can buy and possess cannabis, sold at state-licensed dispensaries. Using it in public or driving under its influence remains illegal.

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need a set of routine immunizations to attend school or child care; New Jersey allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: Carrying a handgun requires a Permit to Carry issued through the State Police, with training and application requirements; buying any firearm requires a purchaser identification card or pistol purchase permit.

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: Yes — New Jersey has a graduated state income tax on wages and other income, filed with the Division of Taxation.

facts.question: How long do I have to transfer my license and registration?
facts.answer: Within 60 days of moving in, or before your current license and registration expire — whichever comes first — through the Motor Vehicle Commission.

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register online, by mail, or in person at least 21 days before an election. New Jersey mails every registered voter information about voting options each election.

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are set and billed by your municipality and fund schools, county, and local services. The state's ANCHOR program pays a property-tax relief benefit to eligible homeowners and renters.

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Jersey law requires a licence to hunt or trap at any age, and anyone over 16 needs one to fish the state's fresh waters with a rod and line. Saltwater fishing is registered separately rather than licensed.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 23:3-1 (Licence for hunting, fishing, trapping)

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Jersey law states a fundamental right to choose whether to carry a pregnancy, to give birth, or to end one. The Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act sets no time limit and requires no waiting period.
facts.sourceOrg: New Jersey Revised Statutes 10:7-2 (Freedom of Reproductive Choice Act)

facts.question: Is marijuana legal?
facts.answer: Recreational marijuana is not legal. Possessing three-quarters of an ounce or less is a civil violation (a fine, not a crime), and a state-run therapeutic cannabis program serves qualifying patients.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What vaccinations do schools require?
facts.answer: Children need routine immunizations to enroll in school or child care; New Hampshire allows medical and religious exemptions with documentation.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: What are the basics of carrying a firearm?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows anyone who may legally own a handgun to carry it openly or concealed without a license. An optional pistol/revolver license exists, mainly for carrying in other states that honor it.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Is there a state income tax?
facts.answer: No — New Hampshire does not tax wages, and its separate tax on interest and dividends was repealed effective 2025. There is also no state sales tax.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How long do I have to register my car and get a license?
facts.answer: New residents have 60 days after establishing residency to register vehicles and get a New Hampshire driver's license. Registration runs through your town clerk plus the DMV.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Division of Motor Vehicles
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do I register to vote, and by when?
facts.answer: Register with your town or city clerk ahead of time, or at the polls on election day itself. Bring proof of who you are, your age, your citizenship, and where you live.
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: How do property taxes work?
facts.answer: Property taxes are the main way New Hampshire towns and schools are funded, set town by town; the annual town meeting votes the budget that drives the rate. Credits and exemptions (veterans, elderly, disabled) run through your town.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration
facts.verification: NH state hosts 403 non-browser clients; page title verified in a real browser 2026-08-14

facts.question: Am I allowed to hunt or fish?
facts.answer: Yes, with a licence. New Hampshire law says nobody may fish, hunt or trap in the state without first getting a valid licence, and it has to be carried while you are doing it. The same chapter sets out the exceptions, including some for young people.

facts.question: What is the law on abortion?
facts.answer: New Hampshire allows abortion up to 24 weeks of pregnancy. From 24 weeks a provider may not perform one except in a medical emergency, and must first determine the likely gestational age. There is no time limit written into state law before that point.
facts.sourceOrg: New Hampshire RSA 329:44 (Fetal Life Protection Act — Prohibition)

Congress Street 1st Floor Tucson, AZ 85701 Public Access to Hearing Room at 4:40 p.m. Board of Supervisors' Hearing Room 5:00 PM Tuesday, July 28, 2026 PIMA COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS Jennifer Allen, Chair, District 3 Dr. Matt Heinz, Vice Chair, District 2 Rex Scott, Member, District 1 Steve Christy, Member, District 4 Andrés Cano, Member, District 5 AGENDA/ADDENDUM AND BROADCAST INFORMATION At least 24 hours before each scheduled meeting, the agenda/addendum is available online at www.pima.gov and in the Clerk of the Board’s Office, 130 W. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Please contact the Clerk of the Board at (520) 724-8449 for these services at least three (3) business days prior to the Board Meeting. Page 1 Pima County Printed on 7/27/2026

          "minutes": "Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated.           "minutes": "Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Meeting Materials Beginning January 13, 2026, Tucson Unified will be using Diligent Community to provide easy access to support materials, greater efficiency for the district, and increased transparency. Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Public access for each meeting will begin 15 minutes prior to the vote to go into Executive Session. Meeting notices are posted outside the front door at the TUSD District Office at 1010 E. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting. The complete rules for Call to the Audience are located in Governing Board Policy BEDH - Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Se observarán los siguientes procedimientos relacionados con la porción del Llamado a la Audiencia: Los miembros del público que deseen abordar a la Mesa Directiva deben llenar la forma Petición para Dirigirse a La Mesa Directiva y someta esta forma electronicamente a la oficina de la Mesa Directiva para el mediodia el dia de la junta, o fisicamente al personal de la Mesa Directiva en la reunión en cualquier momento antes del cierre del Llamado a la Audiencia. Debe incluir su nombre, tema de los comentarios y debe incluir cuál asunto de la agenda se relacionan sus comentarios. Debe indicar si desea dirigirse a la Mesa Directiva en persona o someter sus comentarios escritos para ser leidos (comentarios escritos pueden ser eviados por correo electrónico al [email protected] ) para el mediodia del dia de la junta. Las reglas completes para la Llamado a la Audiencia pueden encontrar en la Política de la Mesa Directiva BEDH – Public Participation at Board Meetings, Policy-Code-BEDH (tusd1.org) . Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible.           "minutes": "Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. It removed all five members of the county's Industrial Development Authority board without cause, approved a new structure for that authority, and elected new members. It also approved the River Overlook rezoning and comprehensive-plan amendment on West River Road (5–0) and two cell-tower permits, updated the county's air-quality code to match current federal rules, denied a wholesale liquor license on East Cabeza De Vaca Street (zoning there does not allow wholesale), and — sitting as the Library District board — accepted a $7,500 grant for a local-news pilot program (4–1), among other business.",

Congress Street, 1st Floor, Tucson, AZ 85701, Mon-Fri, 8am to 5pm. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Clearly print your name/address, the item number and other requested information. Speaker Card(s) are required for Call to the Public and Public Hearing Items. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. The Chair reserves the right to ensure all testimony is pertinent or non-repetitive so matters are handled fairly and expeditiously. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board. HEARING ROOM NOTICE Law permits that a video and/or audio recording of all or part of this meeting may be made if doing so does not interfere with the conduct of the meeting. Pima County has no control over the use and distribution of any such recordings. In addition to the official meeting proceedings, these recordings may include images of and comments made by the public prior to the start, during a recess and after adjournment of the meeting, and may be posted on social media or other internet sites. ACCESSIBILITY The Board Hearing Room is wheelchair and handicapped accessible. Any person who is in need of special services (e.g., assistive listening device, Braille or large print agenda material, signer for hearing impaired, accessible parking, etc.) due to any disability will be accommodated. Cable Channels: Cox 96 Webcast: www.pima.gov PUBLIC PARTICIPATION SPEAKERS ARE LIMITED UP TO 3 MINUTES To address the Board of Supervisors, please complete a Speaker’s Card. Once completed submit your Speaker Card(s) to Clerk staff. When the Chair announces your name, step forward to the podium and state your name for the record. All attendees are advised that the Board of Supervisors strongly adhere to the Board of Supervisors Rules and Regulations. Outbursts, breaches of peace, boisterous conduct or other unlawful interference will result in that individual being asked to leave the meeting room. Any questions pertaining to the meeting can be directed to Melissa Manriquez, Clerk of the Board.           "minutes": "Per the Board's posted meeting-summary report (full minutes post after approval): the Board appointed Jorge Soto as Pima County Treasurer (4–1, one abstention) after a first motion for a different candidate died without a second. Fifth Street, Tucson, AZ 85711. There will be a Public Hearing at the August 25th meeting for the Revision of Instructional Time Model (ITM) for Palo Verde High Magnet School Effective for the 2026-2027 School Year. Tenth Street, Tucson, AZ 85719. Call to the Audience The following procedures related to the Call to the Audience portion of Board meetings will be observed: Members of the public who wish to address the Board shall complete a Request to Address Board form and submit electronically to the Board office by noon the day of the meeting or physically to Board Staff at the start of the meeting before the close of Call to the Audience. Submission must include name of speaker, topic of comments and should indicate which agenda item your comments relate to. Submission must indicate whether individuals will address the Board in person or will submit written comments to be read into the record (email written comments to [email protected] ) by noon the day of the meeting.
